bibl.title: Circular RNA profiling reveals an abundant circHIPK3 that regulates cell growth by sponging multiple miRNAs

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: circular RNAs in human normal and cancerous tissue - A CLASS WHOSE MEMBERS ARE SPLICING ERRORS OR REGULATORS DEPENDING ON WHERE AN ABUNDANCE CUT-OFF IS PUT, and one abundant member of it, circHIPK3
span.quote: Consistent with previous studies of different cell types 11 , 12 , we found that most circRNAs in human normal and cancerous tissues are of low abundance and consequently may be by-products in pre-mRNA splicing. However, certain circRNAs are predominately expressed in one gene locus and present at substantial levels that suggest these species are purposefully produced.

span.label: how many circRNAs there are in human tissue, which of them are abundant enough to be doing something rather than being splicing noise, and what one such circRNA does
span.quote: In total, 67,358 distinct circRNA candidates were found in these tissues and 27,296 of these circRNAs contained at least two unique back-spliced reads ( Fig. 1a , Supplementary Data 1 ). Compared with previously published databases obtained from circBase 9 (92,061 human circRNAs) and a most recent study 10 (65,731 human circRNAs identified mainly from human brain tissues), we found that there are 19,071 overlapped circRNAs and 8,225 novel circRNAs identified in our study ( Supplementary Fig. 2 and Supplementary Data 1 ). Notably, there are totally 148,701 unique human circRNA candidates from all the studies, indicating that circRNAs may contain one of the largest RNA families in human transcription.

span.label: a 13-tissue circRNA profile; the observation that one isoform usually dominates a locus; and the functional characterisation of circHIPK3 as a growth modulator that binds nine miRNAs
span.quote: We further investigated the abundance of the circRNAs within one gene locus, and found that about 50% of the host genes (1,835/3,687, single circRNA from one gene not included) produced a significantly higher expressed circRNAs (at least twofold higher than other circRNAs, Fig. 2b ). This result indicates that there is often a predominantly expressed circRNA isoform from one gene locus.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: A subsequent cell proliferation assay indicated that the downregulation of circHIPK3, but not HIPK3 mRNA, significantly suppressed cell growth in different cell types ( Fig. 5c-e ). An EdU incorporation assay also revealed that the proliferation of various human cells was impaired on the knockdown of circHIPK3 expression ( Fig. 5f,g and Supplementary Fig. 7 ). Consistent with this result from the siRNA knockdown experiments, we observed that cell proliferation was significantly suppressed on the knockdown of circHIPK3 expression in HEK-293 T cells via CRISPR/Cas9 technology ( Supplementary Fig. 8 ). These findings revealed that circHIPK3 may function to modulate the growth of human cells.

span.label: exonic back-splicing - a covalently closed RNA produced from a protein-coding exon, in this case a single 1,099 bp exon of HIPK3 flanked by inverted Alu repeats
span.quote: The genomic structure shows that circHIPK3 contains a large second exon (1,099 bp) from the HIPK3 gene flanked by long introns on either side

span.label: ribosomal-RNA-depleted strand-specific RNA-seq of 6 normal and 7 cancerous human tissues, TopHat2 alignment, 20-nt anchor alignment of the unmapped reads to find head-to-tail junctions, then siRNA/CRISPR knockdown and a 424-miRNA luciferase screen
span.term: ribosomal-RNA-depleted strand-specific RNA-seq of 6 normal and 7 cancerous human tissues, TopHat2 alignment, 20-nt anchor alignment of the unmapped reads to find head-to-tail junctions, then siRNA/CRISPR knockdown and a 424-miRNA luciferase screen
span.quote: Anchor alignments were extended such that the complete read aligns and the breakpoints were flanked by GT/AG splice sites. The total number of reads spanning back-spliced junctions was used as an absolute measure of circRNA abundance.

span.label: THE SAME MOLECULE IS AN ERROR OR A FUNCTION DEPENDING ON A CUT-OFF, AND THE PAPER SAYS BOTH IN ONE SENTENCE: `most circRNAs ... are OF LOW ABUNDANCE and consequently MAY BE BY-PRODUCTS in pre-mRNA splicing. HOWEVER, certain circRNAs are predominately expressed in one gene locus and present at substantial levels that suggest these species are PURPOSEFULLY PRODUCED`. Abundance is doing the ontological work
span.quote: Consistent with previous studies of different cell types 11 , 12 , we found that most circRNAs in human normal and cancerous tissues are of low abundance and consequently may be by-products in pre-mRNA splicing. However, certain circRNAs are predominately expressed in one gene locus and present at substantial levels that suggest these species are purposefully produced.

span.label: and the cut that separates them is stated: `5' CR>0.2; 3' CR>0.2; SRPBM>1` yields `990 HIGH-ABUNDANCE circRNAs` out of 27,296. THE FUNCTIONAL CLASS IS 3.6% OF THE DETECTED CLASS, and the 3.6% is a threshold, not a property
span.quote: When using a stringency of CR and SRPBM cut-off (5′ CR>0.2; 3′ CR>0.2; SRPBM>1), we observed 990 high-abundance circRNAs, many of which were more highly expressed than their linear isoforms

span.label: the formation mechanism is INVERTED REPEAT PAIRING: `two primate-specific Alu elements in an inverted orientation immediately flank the HIPK3 circularizing exon`, and deleting the downstream one abolishes circularisation
span.quote: We observed that circularization was inhibited when the downstream Alu sequence was deleted ( Fig. 4e ). Surprisingly, the deletion of the upstream Alu sequence did not decrease the formation of circHIPK3, rather, it slight increased the formation of this RNA

span.label: and the negative evidence for the competing mechanism is named: `EXON SKIPPING WAS NOT OBSERVED in the HIPK3 gene via either the RNA-seq data or the RT-PCR assay. Thus, the formation of circHIPK3 may be due to DIRECT BACK-SPLICING`. The alternative was looked for with two instruments and not found
span.quote: Notably, exon skipping was not observed in the HIPK3 gene via either the RNA-seq data or the RT–PCR assay. Thus, the formation of circHIPK3 may be due to direct back-splicing with the help of intronic RNA pairings.

span.label: THE PAPER CONCEDES THE GENERAL FORM OF ITS OWN CLAIM: `most recent publications suggest that circRNAs DO NOT NECESSARILY function as miRNA sponges ... Since most of the circRNAs are of low abundance and small length, WE AGREED THAT MANY circRNAs MAY NOT SERVE AS miRNA SPONGES`. A sponging paper agreeing that sponging is usually not the answer, and defending one instance instead
span.quote: Since most of the circRNAs are of low abundance and small length, we agreed that many circRNAs may not serve as miRNA sponges.

span.label: the count of the class is WHATEVER YOU UNION: 67,358 candidates here, 27,296 at the two-read cut, 92,061 in circBase, 65,731 in another study, `148,701 unique human circRNA candidates FROM ALL THE STUDIES`. SIX NUMBERS FOR ONE CLASS, 5.4x apart, all printed in one paragraph
span.quote: In total, 67,358 distinct circRNA candidates were found in these tissues and 27,296 of these circRNAs contained at least two unique back-spliced reads ( Fig. 1a , Supplementary Data 1 ). Compared with previously published databases obtained from circBase 9 (92,061 human circRNAs) and a most recent study 10 (65,731 human circRNAs identified mainly from human brain tissues), we found that there are 19,071 overlapped circRNAs and 8,225 novel circRNAs identified in our study ( Supplementary Fig. 2 and Supplementary Data 1 ). Notably, there are totally 148,701 unique human circRNA candidates from all the studies, indicating that circRNAs may contain one of the largest RNA families in human transcription.

span.label: AND THE ALIGNER DECIDES WHAT EXISTS, on a bare assertion: `we used TopHat2 INSTEAD OF Bowtie2 for the initial mapping because we found THERE MAY RESULT IN FALSE POSITIVE RATE when using Bowtie2`. No rate is given, no comparison is shown, and the choice determines the 67,358
span.quote: Notably, we used TopHat2 instead of Bowtie2 for the initial mapping because we found there may result in false positive rate when using Bowtie2.

span.label: the specificity cut-offs are chosen for their PASS RATE, which the paper states and does not defend: `We used 0.5 (LEAVES 87.5% LEFT OVER) as the cut-off`, and `four reads for the specificity cut-off as this read number LEAVES 99% LEFT OVER`. Honest, and still a decision made by how much survives it
span.quote: The specificity score ranges from 0 to 1, and the mean score is 0.1625. We used 0.5 (leaves 87.5% left over) as the cut-off. We also considered the circRNA abundance with minimum level of mean+2s.d.

span.label: the sponge evidence is a REPORTER assay, not the endogenous transcript: 9 of 424 miRNA mimics reduced luciferase by at least 30% when circHIPK3 sat in a 3'-UTR. The 30% and the 424 are both the screen's, not the cell's
span.quote: Compared with the control RNA, 9 miRNAs (miR-124, miR-152, miR-193a, miR-29a, miR-29b, miR-338, miR-379, miR-584 and miR-654) out of the 424 miRNAs were able to reduce the luciferase reporter activities by at least 30% ( Fig. 6d ). These miRNAs could not significantly decrease circHIPK3 level by qRT–PCR analysis ( Supplementary Fig. 9 ), suggesting that circHIPK3 may not be digested by these miRNAs.

span.label: an siRNA targeting only the back-splice junction, run beside one targeting only the linear transcript and one targeting the shared exon
span.note: eliminates: the objection that a growth effect attributed to the circle is really the gene's - the junction siRNA `knocked down ONLY THE CIRCULAR TRANSCRIPT and did not affect the expression of linear species` · outcome: held
span.quote: As expected, siRNA directed against the backsplice sequence knocked down only the circular transcript and did not affect the expression of linear species ( Fig. 5b ). siRNA targeted to exonic sequences shared by both the linear and circular species effectively knocked down both transcripts

span.label: RNase R digestion and outward-facing (divergent) primers on 36 candidates, plus Sanger sequencing of the products
span.note: eliminates: linear trans-splicing products masquerading as circles - a circle survives an exonuclease and a linear molecule does not · outcome: held

span.label: circHIPK3
span.quote: We further noted that one of these circRNAs, derived from the HIPK3 gene Exon2 (termed circHIPK3), was particularly abundant and featured a high back-spliced ratio ( Fig. 2d , blue dot). The high abundance of circHIPK3 was also observed by previous reports 7 , 17 . Besides circHIPK3, there are another four circRNA isoforms identified in our study in HIPK3 gene locus (We termed them as circHIPK3.2, circHIPK3.3, circHIPK3.4, circHIPK3.5, respectively; Fig. 3a ). circHIPK3 is the predominant circRNA isoform as evidence from the high-supported back-spliced unique reads (circHIPK3, 1880; circHIPK3.2, 30; circHIPK3.3, 7; circHIPK3.4, 6; circHIPK3.5, 2).

span.label: ciRS-7
span.quote: Specifically, the circRNA ciRS-7 (also termed CDR1as), which harbours more than 70 conventional miR-7-binding sites, has been identified as a miRNA inhibitor.

span.label: CDR1as
span.quote: Specifically, the circRNA ciRS-7 (also termed CDR1as), which harbours more than 70 conventional miR-7-binding sites, has been identified as a miRNA inhibitor.

span.label: SRPBM
span.quote: To estimate the relative expression of a circRNA, denoted as SRPBM reads 7 , we counted the total number of reads mapped to the human reference genome in each sample and normalized the number of reads spanning the back-spliced junction to the total number of mapped reads (units in billion) and read length. Therefore, SRPBM=number of circular reads/number of mapped reads (units in billion)/read length.

span.label: CR
span.quote: To estimate the CR of a circRNA at the 5′ end or 3′ end, we counted the number of reads spanning the linear splicing junction and divided the number of reads spanning the back-spliced junction by the total number of reads spanning both the back-spliced junction and linear splicing junction. Therefore, CR=number of circular reads/(number of circular reads+number of linear reads).

span.quote: The specificity score (S) was defined as 1−JSD, which represents for the Jensen–Shannon distance between expression profile of a gene across all tissues and the ‘perfectly specific expression' in a particular tissue.

span.label: `circRNA` - A CLASS THAT IS NOISE AND FUNCTION AT ONCE. `most circRNAs ... are of low abundance and consequently MAY BE BY-PRODUCTS in pre-mRNA splicing. However, certain circRNAs ... suggest these species are PURPOSEFULLY PRODUCED`. Two senses of one term, in one sentence, separated by an abundance threshold

However, certain circRNAs are predominately expressed in one gene locus and present at substantial levels that suggest these species are purposefully produced.

span.quote: We further noted that one of these circRNAs, derived from the HIPK3 gene Exon2 (termed circHIPK3), was particularly abundant and featured a high back-spliced ratio ( Fig. 2d , blue dot). span.label: `ciRS-7` = `CDR1as` - THE SAME MOLECULE UNDER TWO NAMES, given in apposition: `the circRNA ciRS-7 (ALSO TERMED CDR1as)`. One of the two cue shapes the gate can read

span.label: `SRPBM` - `spliced reads per billion mapping`, and the sense IS the formula: `SRPBM=number of circular reads/number of mapped reads (units in billion)/read length`. A unit invented so two RNA-seq runs can be compared at all
span.quote: To estimate the relative expression of a circRNA, denoted as SRPBM reads 7 , we counted the total number of reads mapped to the human reference genome in each sample and normalized the number of reads spanning the back-spliced junction to the total number of mapped reads (units in billion) and read length. span.label: `circular ratio (CR)` - the fraction of junction reads at one end of an exon that are back-spliced: `CR=number of circular reads/(number of circular reads+number of linear reads)`. THE CIRCLE IS DEFINED RELATIVE TO ITS OWN LINEAR COMPETITOR

span.quote: To clarify the specific circRNAs in each cancerous and matched normal tissues, we used Poisson distribution to determine the read number for specificity identification. We profiled the reads for all circRNAs in cancer and normal tissues, respectively. span.quote: We further investigated the abundance of the circRNAs within one gene locus, and found that about 50% of the host genes (1,835/3,687, single circRNA from one gene not included) produced a significantly higher expressed circRNAs (at least twofold higher than other circRNAs, Fig. 2b ). This result indicates that there is often a predominantly expressed circRNA isoform from one gene locus.

span.label: A SPONGING PAPER AGREEING THAT SPONGING IS USUALLY NOT THE ANSWER: `Since most of the circRNAs are of low abundance and small length, WE AGREED THAT MANY circRNAs MAY NOT SERVE AS miRNA SPONGES`

span.quote: Notably, most recent publications suggest that circRNAs do not necessarily function as miRNA sponges in human and mouse cells 10 , 11 , 13 , 20 . Nevertheless, circRNAs in Drosophila reportedly contain conserved miRNA sites 37 . These studies are mainly based on genome-wide bioinformatic analyses of all circRNA candidates and no experimental validations.

span.quote: Notably, exon skipping was not observed in the HIPK3 gene via either the RNA-seq data or the RT–PCR assay. Thus, the formation of circHIPK3 may be due to direct back-splicing with the help of intronic RNA pairings.

span.label: THE FUNCTION IS ASSIGNED TO THE CIRCLE, NOT THE LOCUS: `the downregulation of circHIPK3, BUT NOT HIPK3 mRNA, significantly suppressed cell growth in different cell types`, with a junction-specific siRNA that leaves the linear species intact

span.quote: A subsequent cell proliferation assay indicated that the downregulation of circHIPK3, but not HIPK3 mRNA, significantly suppressed cell growth in different cell types ( Fig. 5c-e ). An EdU incorporation assay also revealed that the proliferation of various human cells was impaired on the knockdown of circHIPK3 expression ( Fig. 5f,g and Supplementary Fig. 7 ). Consistent with this result from the siRNA knockdown experiments, we observed that cell proliferation was significantly suppressed on the knockdown of circHIPK3 expression in HEK-293 T cells via CRISPR/Cas9 technology ( Supplementary Fig. 8 ). These findings revealed that circHIPK3 may function to modulate the growth of human cells.

These miRNAs could not significantly decrease circHIPK3 level by qRT–PCR analysis ( Supplementary Fig. 9 ), suggesting that circHIPK3 may not be digested by these miRNAs.

span.label: and five names coined here in one sentence: circHIPK3, and `We TERMED them as circHIPK3.2, circHIPK3.3, circHIPK3.4, circHIPK3.5, respectively`
span.term: and five names coined here in one sentence: circHIPK3, and `We TERMED them as circHIPK3.2, circHIPK3.3, circHIPK3.4, circHIPK3.5, respectively`
span.quote: We further noted that one of these circRNAs, derived from the HIPK3 gene Exon2 (termed circHIPK3), was particularly abundant and featured a high back-spliced ratio ( Fig. 2d , blue dot). The high abundance of circHIPK3 was also observed by previous reports 7 , 17 . Besides circHIPK3, there are another four circRNA isoforms identified in our study in HIPK3 gene locus (We termed them as circHIPK3.2, circHIPK3.3, circHIPK3.4, circHIPK3.5, respectively; Fig. 3a ). circHIPK3 is the predominant circRNA isoform as evidence from the high-supported back-spliced unique reads (circHIPK3, 1880; circHIPK3.2, 30; circHIPK3.3, 7; circHIPK3.4, 6; circHIPK3.5, 2).

span.label: spliced reads per billion mapping - `SRPBM=number of circular reads/number of mapped reads (units in billion)/read length`. DEFINED AS AN EQUATION, WITH NO DEFINING VERB ANYWHERE IN THE SENTENCE
span.quote: To estimate the relative expression of a circRNA, denoted as SRPBM reads 7 , we counted the total number of reads mapped to the human reference genome in each sample and normalized the number of reads spanning the back-spliced junction to the total number of mapped reads (units in billion) and read length. Therefore, SRPBM=number of circular reads/number of mapped reads (units in billion)/read length.

span.label: circular ratio - `CR=number of circular reads/(number of circular reads+number of linear reads)`, computed separately at the 5' and 3' ends. ALSO AN EQUATION, ALSO WITH NO DEFINING VERB
span.quote: To estimate the CR of a circRNA at the 5′ end or 3′ end, we counted the number of reads spanning the linear splicing junction and divided the number of reads spanning the back-spliced junction by the total number of reads spanning both the back-spliced junction and linear splicing junction. Therefore, CR=number of circular reads/(number of circular reads+number of linear reads).

span.quote: Anchor alignments were extended such that the complete read aligns and the breakpoints were flanked by GT/AG splice sites. The total number of reads spanning back-spliced junctions was used as an absolute measure of circRNA abundance.

span.quote: In total, 67,358 distinct circRNA candidates were found in these tissues and 27,296 of these circRNAs contained at least two unique back-spliced reads ( Fig. 1a , Supplementary Data 1 ). Compared with previously published databases obtained from circBase 9 (92,061 human circRNAs) and a most recent study 10 (65,731 human circRNAs identified mainly from human brain tissues), we found that there are 19,071 overlapped circRNAs and 8,225 novel circRNAs identified in our study ( Supplementary Fig. 2 and Supplementary Data 1 ). Notably, there are totally 148,701 unique human circRNA candidates from all the studies, indicating that circRNAs may contain one of the largest RNA families in human transcription.
